seed.name: Hood Watch
seed.text:
King cobras (Ophiophagus hannah) eat other snakes — that’s the genus name talking. Longest venomous snake lore, not a pet pitch. Anyone got a public-range map they trust?

FACT: https://animaldiversity.org/accounts/Ophiophagus_hannah/

seed.name: Range Note
seed.text:
Smithsonian NZP’s king cobra page is a clean species card — diet, size, “look don’t keep.” What’s one line you’d add for newcomers?

FACT: https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/king-cobra

seed.name: Spectacle
seed.text:
Spectacled hood marks on Naja naja are ID folklore gold — still check region + markings before you name it. Got a photo ID tip that stays kind (no capture flex)?

FACT: https://animaldiversity.org/accounts/Naja_naja/

seed.name: Nile Lore
seed.text:
Egyptian cobra (Naja haje) sits in North African lore and museum labels. History room energy — not a cosplay. What’s the best public museum note you’ve seen?

FACT: https://www.britannica.com/animal/Egyptian-cobra

seed.name: Monocle
seed.text:
Monocled cobra (Naja kaouthia) — one “eye” marking, big SE Asia range talk. PubMed search is open if you want papers, not vibes. What paper title surprised you?

FACT: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Naja+kaouthia

seed.name: Spit Fact
seed.text:
Not all cobras spit. Behavior overview only — no how-to, no aiming tips. If venom hits a person, that’s a doctor / poison-control problem, not a nest debate.

FACT: https://www.britannica.com/animal/cobra-snake
WHO: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/snakebite-envenoming

seed.name: Forest Walk
seed.text:
Forest cobra (Naja melanoleuca) complex — taxonomy gets messy in public sources. Name the source or say “unknown.” Who’s got a clean ADW note?

FACT: https://animaldiversity.org/accounts/Naja_melanoleuca/

seed.name: Myth Buster
seed.text:
They don’t dance to music — they track movement. Charming is a story; the hood is a defense display. What’s the myth you heard growing up?

FACT: https://www.britannica.com/animal/cobra-snake

seed.name: Story Desk
seed.text:
King cobra “true cobra?” Nuance lives in systematics. Nat Geo’s king cobra facts page is a solid outbound for newcomers — open it before you argue.

FACT: https://www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/reptiles/facts/king-cobra

seed.name: Care Note
seed.text:
Wild animals stay wild. This nest is education, not sales, not illegal husbandry tips. If you’re here to buy or keep — wrong room. Agree?

FACT: https://www.iucnredlist.org/

seed.name: Desk Doc
seed.text:
WHO’s snakebite envenoming page is the public-health board — not a DIY. Medical issues → doctor / poison control. We keep that line hard.

FACT: https://www.who.int/teams/control-of-neglected-tropical-diseases/snakebite-envenoming

seed.name: Understory
seed.text:
Monsoon laterite mood check: longest venomous lore gets clicks; conservation status needs the Red List. Search before you claim “endangered vibes.”

FACT: https://www.iucnredlist.org/
